title: Recover from a failed lazy chunk load instead of leaving a broken panel
outcome:
A lazily loaded chunk that fails to fetch leaves the user with a broken panel or with nothing at all, and leaves the server with no record. MEASURED, not inferred.

FOUR PRODUCTION LAZY-LOAD SITES, NONE HANDLING FAILURE:
- ui/src/panels/SourcePanel.tsx:32,35 - React.lazy(() => import("../MonacoCodeEditor")) and MonacoDiffEditor
- ui/src/panels/DiffPanel.tsx:122 - React.lazy(() => import("../MonacoDiffEditor"))
- ui/src/panels/render-edit-file-view.tsx:42 - React.lazy(() => import("../MonacoCodeEditor"))
- ui/src/mermaid-render.ts:507 - await import("mermaid")
Plus ui/src/main.tsx:43-44, two warm-up imports invoked as `void import(...)` with NO catch at all, so a failure there is an unhandled promise rejection and invisible in production.

WHEN THIS HAPPENS: any time the referenced chunk is not in the served tree - a partially copied deploy, a file dropped during copy-over, or (if we ever add one) a retention prune that removed a build a tab was still running. A live probe confirms the server answers 404 for a missing asset, and there is no request logging, so nothing records it either.

WHY THE RECOVERY MATTERS MORE THAN THE RETENTION WINDOW, which is the point worth keeping: neither available signal can ever certify that a build is safe to remove. A 404 on a hashed asset proves a client still needed it; silence proves nothing, because a tab may hold an old graph for hours without touching the missing chunk. A client that reports its own entry identity on connect proves a build is live NOW; its silence proves nothing either, because a frozen or backgrounded tab reports nothing and then wakes - the same lifecycle we already handle in the live-event transport. Both asymmetries point the same way: PRESENCE PROVES USE, ABSENCE NEVER PROVES DISUSE.

So any prune is irreversibly a bet, and the thing to build is a failure that is SAFE WHEN WRONG rather than a window that is right: a failed chunk import should reload onto the current index.html, which is always present. That turns "the user's tab is silently broken" into "the user's tab moves to the current build". It is worth doing on its own, independently of whether a retention policy is ever adopted, because it also covers botched deploys.

Distinguishing the signal, when 404 collection is added: a 404 on a path matching the hashed-asset pattern is categorically different from ordinary 404 noise (bots, stale bookmarks, favicon). It means a client held a valid reference in its graph and the file is gone. One predicate on the path separates evidence from noise.

Design line developed with Engram::Fable; the failing-import inventory above is measured in this repository.
